submitter: bugfix_399_cta_label_agreement lane — bugs_open/399, filed by dartsonline_traffic from an owner report of four broken CTAs; he asked for the general fix, not four individual ones
rationale:
THE DEFECT. setCTAField writes each CTA's destination title to <field>_target_title EXPLICITLY so the content writer can 'write CTA copy FOR the actual destination instead of guessing one' (resolve_internal_links_action.go:335-339). Nothing has ever compared the two. They sit in adjacent keys of one jsonb object, at build time, and no code reads them together. Live on 665 components / 1,191 (label,title,url) triples [MEASURED 2026-08-26].

WHY A CHECK RATHER THAN BETTER PROMPTING — the measurement that decided it, and it could have come out the other way. The writer is ALREADY told twice: cta_text's own llm_guidance in content_components, and at runtime the stamped sentence 'Destination (fixed): <title>. ... never promise a different one' (migrations 476+477, LNK-034). 781 of 2,297 page-content-writer prompts over 3 days carry that literal, and of the pairs written SINCE 477 applied, 155 of 1,060 (14.6%) still contradict their destination [MEASURED 2026-08-26]. Told twice, wrong one time in seven. Prompt text is not a control. (The 23.0%->14.6% before/after split is survivorship-biased, n=135, and is NOT quoted as an effect size anywhere in this change.)

WHY IT RECORDS AND DOES NOT REPAIR OR REFUSE — both were designed and rejected on measurement. REPAIR: of 186 mismatched pairs the copy names exactly one other page in 13, two or more in 78 (RFC_047: refuse, never guess), and NO page at all in 95. A repoint reaches 7% while inheriting bugs_open/248's clobber (a misdirected_cta repair turned a correct /contact.html into a wrong link on 2026-08-24). REFUSAL: at 14.6% it fails ~1 CTA write in 7 (~29 sections/day at the 08-24/25 rate of ~200), nothing can auto-satisfy it, and on a page that re-authors itself daily one cosmetic mismatch becomes an indefinitely withheld refresh.

THE BUG'S OWN FIX CANDIDATE 1 IS REJECTED IN BOTH HALVES, and I want the council to check that reasoning. It proposed comparing the label to _target_title and, on mismatch, regenerating the label from the title. The COMPARISON would be a THIRD definition of 'misdirected' beside the detector's and the writers' — the re-drift RFC_047 s9 rejects by name — and is the shape bugfix_203/CALIBRATION_2026-08-11 measured brittle (nine already-correct CTAs on gaswholesalers.com flipped over a stray hyphen in 'Break-Even'). The REMEDY is worse: regenerating the label from the title is what stampCTADestinationGuidance already asks for, so it converts a mismatch into a LOCK, moving the row out of the ~60 label-less bucket a ranking fix reaches into the ~20 label-locked bucket only an LLM copy pass clears (bugs_open/391).

SO THE CHANGE IS AN EXTRACTION, NOT A NEW MECHANISM. The question already exists and is already answered live — by check_misdirected_cta, but only AFTER render, deploy and a sweep that runs on 1 of 5 discovery agents and demonstrably does not converge (182 misdirected_cta item_keys have been filed more than once). JudgeCTALabel is that same question extracted; ctaClassifyAnchor becomes a thin adaptor over it and its existing tests pass UNCHANGED, which is the proof, and the same bar bugs_open/203's extraction of BestLabelMatch met.

STATED BLIND SPOT, pinned by a test that passes and is wrong on purpose: this cannot see bugs_open/391's label-locked class. When the framework chose the destination AND told the writer to name it, copy and destination AGREE and the button is still wrong (16/17 of that lane's password-entropy fields, including all three buttons the owner reported). Agreement between two framework-written strings is consistency, not correctness.

WHAT I MOST WANT REVIEWED: (1) is record-only the right call, or is the 13-row repoint arm worth its clobber risk; (2) does arming all six save_page_sections steps rather than the obvious two hold up as an INSTRUMENT argument (a biased rate reads fleet-wide); (3) is 'the reading is the rate, not the row' adequately discharged by a RUNBOOK obligation, given bugs_open/410 was filed the same day about records nobody reads.

NOT LISTED AS AN EDIT BECAUSE THE GATE REFUSES COMMENT-ONLY SKETCHES, but it is part of the same commit and reviewers should know: platform/orchestration/datahelpers/label_match.go's BestLabelMatch carries a '⚠ THE CONSUMER SET IS CLOSED' census that its own header requires be kept current. It is updated dated to 2026-08-26 and now reads FOUR call sites, not five — ctaClassifyAnchor stopped being a direct caller when the question it was asking was extracted into JudgeCTALabel, and both read-side consumers now reach the refusal semantics through that one function together rather than one of them silently. Comment-only, no behaviour change.

plan.summary: Extract the misdirected-CTA question into datahelpers.JudgeCTALabel, make the detector a thin adaptor over it, and ask it once more at write time in SavePageSectionsAction's guard chain, recording CTA_LABEL_MISMATCH to agent_error_log. Opt-in, unsafe default OFF. No refusal, no rewrite, no repoint.

edits.rationale: The one shared question, built on the existing BestLabelMatchForPage + LoadCTALabelUniverse. Three-valued so the matcher declining to answer is first-class (RFC_047: an ambiguous label is refused, never guessed) and is reported separately as Ambiguous so 'this button is undecidable' reaches a record rather than nobody. _target_title is deliberately NOT an input: the resolver wrote it from the same pages row LoadCTALabelUniverse reads, so its tokens are already in the candidate's identityTokens, and comparing against it would be a weaker third predicate. SCOPE IS THE CALLER'S and the header says so with a warning: check_cta_nonpage.go:141 feeds ctaClassifyAnchor tel:/mailto: anchors ON PURPOSE, so a ClassifyLinkScope guard inside this function would silently switch off misdirect detection on every phone and email button on the estate — a live check broken without being edited. Caught in design, before code.

Becomes a thin adaptor over JudgeCTALabel so the detector and the write-time audit cannot drift (RFC_047 s9). Behaviour-preserving: check_misdirected_cta_test.go and cta_classify_anchor_test.go pass UNCHANGED, which is the extraction proof and the same bar bugs_open/203 met. check_cta_nonpage reuses this function and converges for free.

edits.rationale: The write-time pass. Opt-in via audit_cta_label_agreement with the unsafe default OFF (owner ruling 2026-08-02). Records to agent_error_log through the shared LogActionEntry writer (RFC_012 B retired the hand-copied INSERT class). NOT a work item: 78 cta_names_unknown_destination + 70 unresolved_cta already sit at needs_human_review with no handler, and bugs_closed/023's closure warns that more detection makes the invisible pile bigger. The label field is read from the component schema via DeriveCTAURLFields and never guessed — the five live pairings include a bare stem (secondary_cta_url<->secondary_cta) and a _label form, so no string rule is right on all of them. A pair is judged only when label, destination AND target title are all present: the title's presence is the scope test that keeps this to the population the bug is about.

One call, in the guard chain beside the link repair. THIS SEAM AND NOT THE RENDER SEAM: RenderComponentAction is where the fresh label first meets the resolved destination and is the WRONG place — RerenderPageSectionsAction bypasses it entirely (rerender_page_sections_action.go:662 calls RenderTemplate directly), so a gate there is blind to the repair loop, which is the loop actually minting the churn. Both writers converge here, verified in live agent_definitions 2026-08-26: page-build-handler -> call_content_writer -> save_sections, and page-rerender -> rerender_sections -> save_sections. Placed AFTER the link repair so it judges the urls that will actually be written.

edits.rationale: Arms the key on ALL SIX live save_page_sections steps, not the obvious two. A recursive census found six: page-build-handler, page-rerender, tool-recreation-handler at top level, and pageflow-builder, page-rebuild, site-work-orchestrator inside a loop's sub_workflow where a top-level {workflow,steps,save_sections} path cannot reach them. This matters MORE for an instrument than a guard: a guard armed on half its writers is visibly partial, an instrument armed on half its writers reports a RATE that reads fleet-wide and is silently biased — and the rate is the whole deliverable. The migration asserts the census is six and aborts otherwise, and verifies with DO/RAISE rather than SELECTs (ON_ERROR_STOP does not abort a COMMIT on a non-empty result set). Post-apply note names the demand control: a pre-roll zero means 'binary not rolled', never 'no mismatches'.
edits.sketch:
BEGIN;

-- Fail loudly if the population has changed since the census above. A migration
-- that silently arms 5 of 7 is how a biased rate ships looking complete.
DO $$
DECLARE
    n integer;
BEGIN
    SELECT count(*) INTO n
    FROM agent_definitions a,
         LATERAL jsonb_path_query(a.default_config,
                 'strict $.**.action ? (@ == "save_page_sections")') x
    WHERE a.is_active AND COALESCE(a.is_snapshot, false) = false AND a.deleted_at IS NULL;

    IF n <> 6 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION
            'save_page_sections step census is %, expected 6 (censused 2026-08-26). '
            'A step was added or removed: re-run the census in this file''s header and '
            'extend the UPDATEs below before arming, or the recorded mismatch RATE is '
            'silently biased by the writers this migration did not reach.', n;
    END IF;
END $$;

-- Top-level save_sections: page-build-handler, page-rerender, tool-recreation-handler.
UPDATE agent_definitions
SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config,
        '{workflow,steps,save_sections,config,audit_cta_label_agreement}', 'true'::jsonb, true),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot, false) = false AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'save_sections'->>'action' = 'save_page_sections';

-- Loop sub_workflows: pageflow-builder, page-rebuild (build_pages_loop).
UPDATE agent_definitions
SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config,
        '{workflow,steps,build_pages_loop,config,sub_workflow,steps,save_sections,config,audit_cta_label_agreement}',
        'true'::jsonb, true),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot, false) = false AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'build_pages_loop'->'config'->'sub_workflow'
        ->'steps'->'save_sections'->>'action' = 'save_page_sections';

-- Loop sub_workflow: site-work-orchestrator (build_items_loop).
UPDATE agent_definitions
SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config,
        '{workflow,steps,build_items_loop,config,sub_workflow,steps,save_sections,config,audit_cta_label_agreement}',
        'true'::jsonb, true),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot, false) = false AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'build_items_loop'->'config'->'sub_workflow'
        ->'steps'->'save_sections'->>'action' = 'save_page_sections';

-- VERIFY as a DO/RAISE, never a bare SELECT: ON_ERROR_STOP does not abort a
-- COMMIT on a non-empty result set, so a SELECT-shaped verify block cannot stop

RFC_047 s10 (owner ruling 2026-08-23) — the undecidable case belongs to an agent that knows the site's premise, not to a token counter; 'until that exists the refusal stands'.

plan.risks:
BLIND TO bugs_open/391's LABEL-LOCKED CLASS BY CONSTRUCTION. When the framework wrote both sides they agree and the button is still wrong. Pinned by TestJudgeCTALabelIsBlindToTheLabelLockedDefect, which passes AND IS WRONG on purpose so no later reader claims coverage this lacks. Stated in the predicate header and the register entry too.

RFC_047 s8.3's residual is inherited unchanged: a CONFIDENT false match is not caught ('See how each brand differs, spec by spec' -> /about.html on an identity-token win). This change neither worsens nor fixes it; it now shows up in a record before deploy rather than only after.

POPULATION LIMIT: only components the resolver covers carry a _target_title, so this sees the six ctaFieldNames components and no others. system-stats (5 rows), tool-cta (5), featured-content (4), tool-llm-cost-calculator (4), tool-list (3) carry CTA url keys and zero titles [MEASURED 2026-08-26] and remain unresolved_cta / bugs_open/389 territory. Stated in the code header so coverage is not assumed.

SITE CHROME IS OUT OF SCOPE: site_components carries no cta/target_title keys and render_site_components_action.go:203 hardcodes 'Get Started'. Governed by STY-053/STY-058; a separate bug, not silently included.

THE READING IS THE RATE, NOT THE ROW, and today that is a paper promise. A monthly query and obligation live in the lane RUNBOOK and the register entry, and both name bugs_open/410 (filed 2026-08-26 about seams that complete green and land somewhere nobody reads) as the class this inherits. I consider this the weakest part of the change and say so rather than hiding it.

ONE NEW PER-PAGE DB READ (component input_schema) on the save path, bounded by page component count, behind the opt-in key, and returning empty on any failure. The pass can never fail a save.

DeriveCTAURLFields is OBSERVE-ONLY at both writers (council trail 2525f980, stage 2 never inverted). This uses it for a READ in a recording pass only — it decides no write, and cannot; flagged here rather than left for a reviewer to find.

SEQUENCING: bugfix_389_cta_relevance's step 4 re-resolves ~60 label-less fields, writing new urls under old generic copy — contradictions BY CONSTRUCTION. That lane has been told directly so the window is read as expected rather than as damage.
